custom_logic_notes: The TrendlessAG_Hist custom indicator is the core signal source. It uses CXMA (from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) with two smoothing passes: first smoothing with XMA_Method1/EMA, XLength1=7, XPhase1=15 applied to a custom price (IPC=PRICE_CLOSE), then a percentage normalization around +-100% (In100=90%), then second smoothing with XMA_Method2/JJMA, XLength2=5, XPhase2=100. The EA reads 3 consecutive values from buffer 0 of this indicator to detect histogram direction changes and crossovers. OnInit() always returns INIT_FAILED (line 95) which appears to be a bug - should be INIT_SUCCEEDED. Trade functions (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose) come from TradeAlgorithms.mqh. LoadHistory() call ensures bar history is available. GlobalVariableDel_() on deinit cleans up global variables.
external_dependencies: SmoothAlgorithms.mqh - CXMA class for multi-method smoothing (JJMA, VIDIA, AMA etc.)
TradeAlgorithms.mqh - BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, LoadHistory
TrendlessAG_Hist - Custom indicator loaded via iCustom()
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement the TrendlessAG_Hist indicator in Python. It requires: (1) Custom price calculation from Applied_price_ enum (9 price types including Demark and TrendFollow), (2) First smoothing pass using XMA/EMA period=7, (3) Percentage normalization to +-100% range with In100=90 threshold, (4) Second smoothing pass using JJMA period=5 phase=100. The JJMA (Jurik Moving Average) algorithm is complex and requires a dedicated implementation. Trade logic is straightforward: histogram rising (Value[1]<Value[2]) with current value above previous (Value[0]>Value[1]) = buy; histogram falling (Value[1]>Value[2]) with current value below previous (Value[0]<Value[1]) = sell. Signal reversal closes opposite positions. Fixed SL=1000 points, TP=2000 points. Note the INIT_FAILED bug in OnInit() line 95 - this EA would never actually run in MT5 as-is.
